facts.value: In general, legal systems can be split between civil law and common law systems. Modern scholars argue that the significance of this distinction has progressively declined. The numerous legal transplants, typical of modern law, result in the sharing of many features traditionally associated with either common law or civil law. The third type of legal system is religious law, based on scriptures.

facts.value: The specific system by which a country is ruled is often determined by its history, its connections with other countries, or its adherence to international standards.

facts.value: The sources that jurisdictions adopt as authoritatively binding are the defining features of any legal system.
